_README: HSF VOTER GUIDE - BASE FILE (configuration and legal copy)
This file holds everything volunteers must NOT touch: settings, the paid-for
disclaimer, publisher name, methodology note, category labels, county list,
ballot level order, and theme colors.
data.base.json     (this file)  - config and legal copy. Editor-owned.
data.content.json               - races, entries, organizations. Comes from the Google Sheet.
data.json          (generated)  - the two above merged. This is what the site reads.
Never hand-edit data.json. Edit this file or the sheet, then re-run the converter.
counties lists all 15 Arizona counties. This is the MASTER list the
converter validates against. data.json only carries the counties that
actually have published content, so voters never hit an empty filter.
Replace every TODO in settings before publishing.
Validate edits before publishing - one missing comma blanks the site.

settings.tagline: Hold the Line. Seize New Ground. Fight Like Hell.
settings.paid_for_by: Paid for by Hold Seize Fight. With 0% from out-of-state contributors. Not Authorized by a Candidate.
settings.methodology_note: Hold Seize Fight selects candidates based on incumbents or candidates for office who embrace justice, democracy, and equality. Entries are researched from campaign materials, public records, and endorsements from allied organizations, then written and reviewed by volunteers before publication. To suggest a correction or a candidate we've missed, write to hsfvote@gmail.com.

propositions.intro: All eight measures on this year's ballot were referred by the legislature, not by citizen petition. Hold Seize Fight recommends a NO vote on every one.

items.title: Ban on vehicle-miles-traveled taxes
items.summary: Writes a transportation funding ban into the Constitution, cutting off road and infrastructure revenue and leaving no room to adapt as needs change.

items.title: Restrictions on public institution programs
items.summary: Bars public schools from any policy referencing race, gender, or sexual orientation, putting lawful mentoring, outreach, and student support programs at risk.

items.title: Voter ID and proof of citizenship requirements
items.summary: Requires photo ID and proof of citizenship for every ballot, including mail ballots, forcing Arizonans to file ID paperwork with the government at every election.

items.title: Cap on local grocery tax
items.summary: Strips local control over taxes and hands it to the state, hitting rural and smaller communities hardest and threatening libraries, parks, and basic services.

items.title: Drug cartels as terrorist organizations
items.summary: A symbolic designation with no enforcement mechanism and no funding to carry it out.

items.title: Student athletics and facility requirements
items.summary: A blanket sports ban written by politicians that treats kindergarteners like college athletes and exposes school teams to lawsuits.

items.title: Photo-enforcement voter approval
items.summary: Blocks local governments from using red-light cameras and other photo enforcement that reduce traffic deaths.

items.title: Legislative control of school budgets
items.summary: Takes budget decisions away from local schools and cuts funding for districts that miss an arbitrary spending threshold set by a state appointee.

categories.blurb: Incumbents in office who are doing the work. Defend these seats.
Candidates committed to going further than the seat's current occupant.
